extracted.intended_audience: community members, community-based organizations, and advocates preparing environmental justice (EJ) public comments during NEPA processes (especially for DOE actions)
extracted.subtask_short: writing EJ public comments for NEPA
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for communities and advocates on drafting effective environmental-justice-focused public comments during NEPA processes, specifying substantive elements to include, procedural stages to target, and participation/access requirements. Emphasizes documentation, data sources, alternatives, and meaningful engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the affected community
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the affected community — demographic data on race, income, language access
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete demographic information to show who is affected (race/ethnicity, income levels, languages spoken) so agencies can see which populations are implicated by the proposed action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document existing burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: Document existing burdens — cumulative pollution, health disparities, prior contamination
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show baseline conditions and historical harms (e.g., local pollution sources, documented health disparities, legacy contamination) to contextualize additional impacts from the proposed action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify disproportionate impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify disproportionate impacts — how the proposed action affects this community vs. others
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare impacts across communities to demonstrate disproportionate effects (quantitative where possible), explaining why burdens fall more heavily on the affected community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand alternative analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Demand alternative analyses — alternative locations, technologies, mitigation measures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request that the NEPA analysis evaluate feasible alternatives (different siting, technologies, or mitigation) and explain why proposed alternatives would reduce or avoid harms to the affected community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference EJSCREEN data
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference EJSCREEN data — EPA's environmental justice screening tool
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite EJSCREEN outputs and explain how screening indicators (e.g., pollution burden, demographic indices) support claims about environmental justice concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite executive orders
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference relevant federal policy and directives (such as EO 12898 on environmental justice and EO 14008) to anchor legal/policy claims about the need to address EJ in the NEPA analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight cumulative impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight cumulative impacts — aggregation across pollution sources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the proposed action adds to existing contamination or pollution from other sources, and request a cumulative impacts analysis rather than treating impacts in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand meaningful engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Demand meaningful engagement — language access, time/place accessibility, in-person hearings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insist on engagement practices that enable full participation (translation/interpretation, accessible meeting locations and times, in-person opportunities) and document any gaps in outreach or accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document community assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Document community assets — cultural sites, sacred lands, traditional ecological knowledge
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe non-economic values and assets (cultural resources, sacred sites, traditional ecological knowledge) that should be considered in the NEPA analysis and protected from adverse impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Comment Effectiveness — reading, acknowledgement, and consolidated responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Public comments must be read and acknowledged by the agency, but agencies can produce one response that addresses several related comments together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that agencies are required to consider and acknowledge comments; organizing and grouping related comments can be efficient but ensure your substantive points are clearly stated so they are captured in the agency response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NEPA as a tool to require consideration of impacts and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: NEPA requires the government to consider the environmental impacts of major federal actions and give the public a chance to comment; it empowers individuals to communicate directly with federal agencies and offer alternatives to proposed actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame comments to trigger NEPA duties: document foreseeable impacts, propose reasonable alternatives, and request analyses the agency must consider under NEPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Participation Requirements — full, fair, and meaningful participation
rubrics_metrics.description: A core principle of EJ is the full and fair participation by all affected communities in the decision-making process; the EJ portion of NEPA aims to foster meaningful participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for procedures and outreach that ensure participation from all affected groups; document barriers to participation and request remedies (e.g., outreach, translation, scheduling) in comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stages for Comment — target appropriate NEPA stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Stages for Comment: Scoping (early - frame the analysis); Draft EIS (substantive analysis comments); Final EIS / Record of Decision (preserve for litigation); Permit/license stage (specific to facility approval).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments at the stage that best fits your objective: use scoping to shape what gets analyzed, Draft EIS to critique analyses and propose alternatives, Final EIS/ROD comments to create a record for potential challenges, and permit-stage comments for project-specific approvals.
